items.title: Tom Brown Interview, 1956
items.q: The transcript mentions 'Art' only in the interviewer's address ('Well, Art, they all say...'). The interviewee (Tom Brown) does not mention Art, nor does he describe any personal interaction, collaboration, or relationship with him.

ctx.x: There's a big ballyhoo today. Would you like to meet the man that started jazz? He's right here in your city standing fast. You shouldn't believe a word of what you've already heard. They're busy telling lies of what they've heard. Tom Brown started jazz in Chicago, even built the name for jazz. Jazz was never used to music until Brown gave it its advance. The colors are not responsible as the great big ballyhoo. It was done by the north, the kid the south. The colors only play plantation and jazz is the part of…
Well, Art, they all say that I was the one that took the first Dixieland band to Chicago.

So it must be so. This band was later turned into jazz by Chicago local musicians. Well, we had the finest kind of tempo and rhythm that took the world by surprise and started something really big. That it is all over the world today. I've enjoyed the fruits of jazz since 1950. I made a lot of photograph records which have made hits. I've made some good records with Yerkes. Yerkes, Dance Orchestra. Yerkes, Happy Six. Yerkes, Southern Five. Yerkes, Jazz Marimba Orchestra. Ray Miller's Black and White Melody Boys.…
